scene-u01-pnew1-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew1-5.text: The channel lets one bit affect later samples: three consecutive bits set one observation vector, giving $8$ clusters

scene-u01-pnew1-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew1-6.text: How to read: bottom to top, three bits are weighted and summed into two samples, forming the observation vector; the table lists the eight bit triples and their centers in the plane.

scene-u01-pnew1-8.name: text#8
scene-u01-pnew1-8.text: Intersymbol interference (ISI): how bits mix into samples

scene-u01-pnew1-43.name: text#43
scene-u01-pnew1-43.text: Three consecutive bits have $2^3=8$ combinations, so $8$ clusters

scene-u01-pnew1-118.name: text#118
scene-u01-pnew1-118.text: "The equalizer must first estimate the channel $f$" is not necessary: send known bits in training and record each cluster center.

scene-u01-pnew1-120.name: text#120
scene-u01-pnew1-120.text: Eight centers from source; triples listed by code

scene-u01-pnew2-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew2-5.text: An ambiguous observation: nearest is $\omega_4$, the nearest other-class $\omega_8$ is only $0.0528$ farther

scene-u01-pnew2-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew2-6.text: How to read: the left is the $(x_k,x_{k-1})$ plane; eight dots are cluster centers (blue: class $B$, orange: class $A$), the green dot is an observation; the right gives distances to the nearest centers and point-wise error rates.

scene-u01-pnew2-8.name: text#8
scene-u01-pnew2-8.text: Eight cluster centers and one observation

scene-u01-pnew2-62.name: text#62
scene-u01-pnew2-62.text: Distances to the three nearest centers

scene-u01-pnew2-84.name: text#84
scene-u01-pnew2-84.text: Nearest is $\omega_4$, giving $I_k=0$; but the nearest $A$ cluster $\omega_8$ is only $0.0528$ farther, so a bit more noise flips it.

scene-u01-pnew2-92.name: text#92
scene-u01-pnew2-92.text: The nearest $A$ and $B$ centers are only $0.5$ apart, so errors rise fast with noise

scene-u01-pnew3-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew3-5.text: Only $16$ transitions are legal: the last two bits of the new triple inherit the first two of the old

scene-u01-pnew3-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew3-6.text: How to read: the left column is the eight clusters at time $k$, the right at $k+1$; each cluster sends only two arrows, and same-colored clusters point to the same two targets.

scene-u01-pnew3-8.name: text#8
scene-u01-pnew3-8.text: Each of eight clusters has two legal next steps

scene-u01-pnew3-93.name: text#93
scene-u01-pnew3-93.text: Same color: same pair of targets; this is why KP07 can reduce eight clusters to four states

scene-u01-pnew3-98.name: text#98
scene-u01-pnew3-98.text: Only $d$ is the newly sent bit, $0$ or $1$

scene-u01-pnew3-105.name: text#105
scene-u01-pnew3-105.text: Such as: $\omega_2=(0,0,1)$ goes to $(d,0,0)$, that is $\omega_1$ or $\omega_5$

scene-u01-pnew3-109.name: text#109
scene-u01-pnew3-109.text: The source gives $\omega_1$ or $\omega_5$ as next steps of $\omega_5,\omega_6$, apparently copied; by the rule they should be $\omega_3$ or $\omega_7$ (and $\omega_4$ or $\omega_8$ for $\omega_7,\omega_8$).

scene-u01-pnew3-111.name: text#111
scene-u01-pnew3-111.text: [Source issue] Derived by rule, enumerated by code
